title: Where CRR stands

data.source: The status cards written by the thirteen mm- rooms of this library (2026), each beside its own framework; CRR's row follows the Phoenix record.

prediction: Set beside thirteen other mathematical metaphysics on nine plain criteria, CRR is strongest on saying what it has not shown, and weakest on everything that needs other people: outside proof, a passed test, replication, a literature.
baseline: The thirteen status cards of the mm- rooms (2026), on one scale; most framework lines are from memory.
why: A table of judgements is not a test. All four of my expectations of the table held. CRR's row follows Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass, an empty result ledger, and no `fits` in tonight's library. The growing block stays ONTOLOGY. It would become a test if the scores were set blind by people who know each field.

criteria: core results proved by people other than the proposer
makes a prediction that differs from the standard model of some field
such a prediction has been tested
peer-reviewed literature, and its rough size

scale.precise_core: 0 none; 1 informal, or precise only in fragments; 2 precise, with free or disputed parts; 3 precise and settled
scale.proved_by_others: 0 nobody else; 1 only close collaborators; 2 a few independent groups; 3 a broad independent community
scale.differing_prediction: 0 none; 1 only vague, or only through an added bridge or side theory; 2 one clear quantitative one; 3 several sharp ones
scale.tested: 0 never; 1 informally or in a toy; 2 a serious test, mostly by the proposing side; 3 serious tests by independent or adversarial groups
scale.passed: 0 nothing passed, or nothing tested; 1 mixed or disputed; 2 one clear pass; 3 repeated clear passes
scale.replicated: 0 none; 1 partial or by allied groups; 2 by one independent group; 3 by many
scale.literature: 0 none known; 1 tens of papers; 2 hundreds; 3 thousands
scale.engineering: 0 none; 1 demonstrations or descendants only; 2 some real use; 3 everyday use
scale.admits_open_problems: 0 denies them; 1 grudging; 2 states them; 3 keeps a public list of them and of its failures

rows.name: Causal set theory: classical sequential growth
reasons: Causal sets and the growth conditions are defined exactly; the family of solutions is a theorem.
A small community, with results on percolation limits by outside mathematicians (Brightwell and Georgiou).
Sorkin's heuristic forecast of a small fluctuating cosmological constant of the observed order; Lorentz-invariant "swerves".
The constant was measured in 1998. Detailed "everpresent Lambda" models have been set against cosmological data.
The order of magnitude matched. The argument is heuristic and the detailed models are disputed.
The measurement is well replicated. The link from it to causal sets is not an independent result.
Hundreds of papers.
None.
Its reviews say plainly that the quantum dynamics is unknown and that most large orders do not look like spacetime.

rows.name: The free energy principle and active inference
reasons: Exact in the linear Gaussian case. The general derivation from a Markov blanket has been disputed in print.
Several independent groups have re-derived, corrected and criticised it (Biehl, Aguilera, Millidge, Buckley and others).
The principle itself makes none. Process theories built on it, such as predictive coding, do. Phoenix gives it the same logical status as CRR's grammar.
The process theories are tested widely in neuroscience; one study tested the principle on neurons in a dish.
Mixed. Misses are usually absorbed as a wrong generative model.
Parts of predictive coding replicate. Nothing specific to the principle has been independently replicated, as far as this check knows.
Thousands of papers.
Dynamic causal modelling is everyday brain-imaging analysis; active inference agents and robots exist as demonstrations.
Its authors publish replies and repairs; whether the principle can fail at all is still argued.

rows.name: Integrated information theory
reasons: Phi is defined exactly within each version, but the definition has changed four times and critics have shown it is not unique.
Independent groups compute, vary and criticise the measures (Barrett, Seth, Mediano, Oizumi, Aaronson).
It differs clearly from workspace theories on where and how consciousness shows in the brain. Its sharpest claims need a phi that cannot be computed for a brain.
A pre-registered adversarial collaboration with a rival theory (results reported from 2023). Phoenix calls it the one metaphysics-adjacent theory to have submitted to such a test.
Mixed: some predictions held and some failed, for both theories. Phoenix records "mixed".
The perturbational complexity index, which IIT inspired, replicates across clinics. It is not phi.
Several hundred papers at least.
The complexity index is used in research on patients who cannot respond. Phi itself is used for nothing.
It states that phi is intractable. Critics say its central claims are shielded from test; its authors dispute that.

rows.name: Whitehead's process philosophy, as a net of occasions
reasons: A scheme of categories in prose. Only fragments have been made exact, chiefly his geometry of regions.
Others built the mathematics of regions and connection from his sketch. Nothing in the metaphysics is the kind of thing one proves.
The metaphysics makes none. His separate 1922 theory of gravity did. Phoenix: "the metaphysics fixed none".
Only the gravity theory was tested.
The gravity theory is generally held to have failed (Will 1971). Phoenix: "the only part of Whitehead that could fail, did".
Nothing to replicate.
A very large philosophical literature over nearly a century, with its own journals.
A descendant only: the calculus of regions used in spatial reasoning grew from his theory of extension.
He called the scheme speculative and open to revision. It names no particular open problems.

rows.name: Constructor theory
reasons: Its principles are stated carefully and some papers are exact; the general theory is still a programme.
Nearly all of it is by Deutsch, Marletto and close collaborators.
A proposed witness: if gravity can entangle two masses it is not classical. This is a test design more than a number.
Photon experiments have acted out some of its arguments. The gravity experiment has not been done.
Nothing that differs from standard quantum theory has been tested.
None.
Tens of papers.
None.
Its authors describe it as unfinished and say what is missing.

rows.name: Assembly theory
reasons: The index is defined exactly. What it measures that older compression measures do not is disputed.
Outside groups have analysed the index and its cost of computation, several of them as critics.
A threshold: molecules above an index of about 15, found in quantity, come only from life.
Mass-spectrometry tests on mixed samples, some blinded, by the proposing group.
Passed in the proposers' test; critics have offered non-living counter-examples.
Repeated with other instruments by the same and allied groups.
Tens of papers, one of them in Nature (2023), and a growing number of replies.
Proposed for life-detection instruments and for chemical search. Not yet in use.
The technical papers state limits (the index is hard to compute; the threshold is empirical). Public claims have been broader and the dispute is sharp.

rows.name: Relational quantum mechanics
reasons: Its mathematics is that of quantum theory, which is exact. What is special to it is stated in prose, with one partial reconstruction from postulates.
Reconstructions and no-go arguments by independent authors (Hoehn and Wever; Brukner; Pienaar; Adlam).
None, by design: it is an interpretation and predicts what quantum mechanics predicts.
Nothing special to it can be tested. Quantum mechanics itself has passed every test, small Wigner's-friend experiments included.
Not applicable: nothing of its own was at risk.
Not applicable.
Hundreds of papers.
None of its own.
It was publicly revised in 2022 in answer to its critics, on how the facts of different systems connect.

rows.name: The block universe with a thermodynamic arrow
reasons: Relativity and statistical mechanics; the fluctuation theorems are theorems.
A broad community over many decades.
The fluctuation theorems forecast how often entropy runs backwards in small systems, against the plain second law. The block READING adds nothing testable to the physics.
Colloidal beads in traps, single molecules pulled apart, small circuits.
Repeatedly.
By many independent laboratories.
Thousands of papers.
Free-energy estimates in molecular simulation use these theorems; satellite navigation uses relativity.
Why the early universe had low entropy (the "past hypothesis") is openly debated and unsolved.

rows.name: Presentism, the growing block and the moving spotlight
reasons: The logic of tenses is exact mathematics. The theses about what exists are stated in prose.
Temporal logic has a broad community of logicians and computer scientists.
None. Phoenix says of the growing block: "difficult direct empirical discrimination".
Never; there is nothing to test.
Not applicable.
Not applicable.
A very large philosophical literature since 1908.
A descendant only: temporal logic, which grew from the logic of tenses, is used to verify chips and software. The ontology is used for nothing.
The standard objections (how do you know it is now; the clash with relativity) are part of the literature itself.

rows.name: Process theories and traced monoidal categories
reasons: Category theory: definitions and theorems.
A broad community of mathematicians and computer scientists.
None. It is a language for composing processes, not a claim about the world.
Not applicable.
Not applicable.
Not applicable.
Hundreds of papers on process theories and string diagrams; far more on category theory at large.
Diagram calculi are used to simplify quantum circuits and to design some software tools.
As in any branch of mathematics, open questions are stated as such.

rows.name: Rosen's (M,R)-systems and autopoiesis
reasons: The (M,R) scheme is defined with sets and maps. Rosen's main theorem, that such systems cannot be simulated, is disputed. Autopoiesis is prose with computer models.
Worked over by independent groups (Letelier, Cardenas, Cornish-Bowden; Louie; Mossio) and by critics.
That organisms cannot be simulated by any machine. It is not stated in a form that can be measured.
Not tested.
Not applicable.
Not applicable.
Hundreds of papers; autopoiesis is very widely cited, mostly as an idea.
Artificial-chemistry and protocell models; an influence on robotics. No everyday use.
Its literature argues openly about whether the central theorem holds.

rows.name: The specious present and duration, as window models
reasons: James and Bergson gave no mathematics, and Bergson held that duration cannot be measured. The scores below are for the window models that descend from them.
Window and frame models have been analysed and fitted by many laboratories.
Frames predict that perception depends on the phase of the brain's own rhythm at the moment of input; a smooth window predicts that it does not.
A long line of experiments on fusion, order and rhythm phase, by many groups.
Integration windows at several time scales are among the firmer findings of the field. The frames version has a mixed record.
The windows replicate widely. Phase effects have both replications and failures.
Thousands of papers, experimental and philosophical.
Film frame rates and audio coding rest on measured integration windows. Nothing is built on James or Bergson as such.
Whether perception is continuous or discrete is treated as open in its own reviews.

rows.name: Rewriting pictures of physics: cellular automata and hypergraphs
reasons: Rewriting systems and causal invariance are defined exactly. The limit object, and the claimed derivations of relativity and quantum theory, are not yet rigorous.
Mostly the project's own members. The older mathematics it draws on (confluence of rewriting systems) is standard and widely shared.
Suggestions only, such as a dimension of space that varies or a top speed for entanglement. No number has been fixed.
Not tested.
Not applicable.
Not applicable.
Tens of papers, many in the project's own journal and reports. The literature on cellular automata in general is far larger.
A descendant only: cellular automata gave rise to lattice methods for fluid flow. The physics project itself is used for nothing.
The technical documents list open problems. Critics say the public account runs well ahead of the mathematics.

rows.name: CRR as given (R1 to R6)
reasons: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status_table.note: Scores 0 to 3. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight.

forks.weighting tests more than literature: not run; it would move the block universe and the window models further ahead and change nothing at CRR's end

result: Totals out of 27: block + arrow 25, windows 19, causal sets 16, free energy 16, IIT 16, assembly 14, process maths 12, views of time 11, Whitehead 10, Rosen 10, relational QM 9, CRR 9, constructor 8, rewriting 7. CRR scores 3 on admitting its open problems, where the middle framework scores 2.0 and none scores higher. It scores 0 on outside proof, passed tests, replication and literature, where the middle frameworks score 2.0, 0.0, 0.0 and 2.0. Its nearest neighbour on the card is constructor (distance 5) and its farthest is block + arrow (distance 18). Of the thirteen rooms, 6 restate, 6 are untestable, 1 is partly and 0 fail; none fits. I wrote 67 predictions in them and 62 held. 115 of the 117 framework card lines are from memory.
